meta.price_basis: All monetary parameters are expressed in real 2024 money (internal unit: USD-2024) in the currency given by each parameter's 'currency' tag (EUR unless stated). Source values published in earlier price years were inflated to 2024 using euro-area HICP (EUR2015 x1.245, EUR2019 x1.21, EUR2020 x1.20, EUR2022 x1.09) or US CPI-U (USD2019 x1.23, USD2020 x1.21, USD2022 x1.07); the factor used is stated in each note. Cost-year basis: nth-of-a-kind European plant commissioned ~2030.
meta.currency_note: Internal model unit is real USD-2024 (was CHF through v7). Values are converted from their tagged currency at meta.fx_to_usd on load. EUR reporting columns use the inverse 2024 rate (USD->EUR 0.9239).
meta.no_ghost_number_note: Each numerical input carries a public source URL and a derivation note. Parameters without a harmonised public source are labelled 'internal screening assumption' and carry a wide range so the uncertainty sampling reflects their status.
meta.no_hidden_credit_note: No co-product or by-product credit is subtracted from delivered cost in the base model. coproduct_credit_chf_per_tonne_saf is retained explicitly at zero.
meta.v7_note: v7 replaces the v6 'USD relabelled as CHF 1:1' convention (review finding P16) with tagged currencies and explicit 2024-average FX. Parameter values are re-sourced to 2024-2026 literature for a ~2030 EU nth-of-a-kind plant; process physics (electrolyser efficiency, DAC energies, FT efficiency) are now sampled parameters; H2 seasonal storage is priced by geology (salt cavern vs lined rock cavern, see country_finance.json); missing cost terms added: raw+demineralised water net of DAC water recovery, airport receiving/fuel-farm adder, rail transport option, battery lifetime distinct from PV/wind, electrolyser stack replacement retained. The previous input set is preserved unchanged in literature_inputs_v6.json for A/B runs.

fx_to_usd.rates_as_of: 2024 annual average ECB reference rates (USD/EUR 1.0824; implied USD/CHF 0.8801 -> CHF/USD 1.1362). Sources: https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/policy_and_exchange_rates/euro_reference_exchange_rates/html/index.en.html ; https://www.estv.admin.ch/de/jahresmittelkurs-wpe

meta.v8_note: v8 additions: (1) full USD-2024 internal basis (parameter keys renamed _chf->_usd; v6/v7-era files remain loadable via aliases); (2) carbon-sourcing block - purchased biogenic CO2 (RFNBO-eligible under Del. Reg. (EU) 2023/1185 Annex pt. 10(c)) with distance-based delivery cost vs on-site DAC; (3) seasonally flexible plant: synthesis minimum-load and finished-fuel tank storage parameters (no seasonal H2 store in the v3 design; islanded plants face no EU temporal-correlation requirement, Del. Reg. (EU) 2023/1184 Art. 3); (4) capex economies-of-scale exponents for mandate-driven plant sizing (see scale.py); (5) mandate demand data in policy_demand.json + airport_fuel.csv. A 2050 technology overlay ships as literature_inputs_2050.json.
meta.overlay_note: 2050 TECHNOLOGY-COST OVERLAY: identical to the v8 2030 file except the parameters listed here, re-based to 2050 projections from the SAME source families (DEA catalogues, Fasihi et al. 2019, Seymour et al. 2024, NREL 2025, SRIA). Non-technology parameters (WACC, logistics, water, carbon logistics, indirects) are held at 2030 values - financing and logistics do not 'learn' comparably. Use with --inputs 2050 for 2050-mandate runs; pair with --inputs v8 to isolate the pure scale/demand effect.

pv_capex_usd_per_kw.source: 2050 OVERLAY: DEA 2050 utility PV: 293 EUR2020/kW_AC (253-400) ~ 352 EUR2024; PyPSA 2050: 368 EUR2025. EUR2024. || 2030 entry: Danish Energy Agency Technology Data (utility PV 2030: 0.384 MEUR2020/MW_AC = ~461 EUR2024/kW); Fraunhofer ISE LCOE 2024 (German utility PV today: 700-900 EUR2024/kWp); JRC CETO PV in the EU 2024 (~EUR 460/kWp expectation 2024); PyPSA technology-data 2030 compilation 482 EUR2025/kW. IRENA RPGC 2024 global weighted average USD 691/kW marks the floor.

wind_capex_usd_per_kw.source: 2050 OVERLAY: DEA 2050 onshore: 963 EUR2020/kW (796-1193) ~ 1156 EUR2024. EUR2024. || 2030 entry: Fraunhofer ISE LCOE 2024 (German onshore 1300-1900 EUR2024/kW); DEA Technology Data 2030 (1.0356 MEUR2015/MW = ~1290 EUR2024/kW); PyPSA technology-data 2030: 1383 EUR2025/kW; JRC CETO Wind 2025 global 2030 ~841 USD2024/kW marks the floor. v6 base 1800 sat at the top of the European evidence and v6 max 3260 had no onshore support.

fom_pv.units: fraction of PV capex per year
fom_pv.source: JRC CETO PV 2024: EU utility O&M 6.8-14.8 EUR/kWp/y; Fraunhofer ISE 2024: 13.3 EUR/kW/y; DEA 2030: 9.5 EUR2020/kW/y. At base capex 520 EUR/kW the base fraction equals ~10.4 EUR/kW/y.

fom_wind.units: fraction of wind capex per year
fom_wind.source: Fraunhofer ISE 2024: 32 EUR/kW/y fixed + 0.007 EUR/kWh variable (~50 EUR/kW/y all-in); DEA 2030: ~17-18 EUR/kW/y all-in. Base 2.6% x 1350 EUR/kW = 35 EUR/kW/y. v6 3.5% of 1800 (=63 EUR/kW/y) exceeded modern full-service benchmarks.

battery_capex_usd_per_kwh.units: per kWh, turnkey utility-scale (2-8 h systems), energy basis
battery_capex_usd_per_kwh.source: 2050 OVERLAY: NREL 2025 update, 2050 4-h systems: 108/178/307 USD2024/kWh; DEA/PyPSA 2050 components ~100 EUR/kWh + 80 EUR/kW. Converted to EUR2024-equivalent band. EUR2024. || 2030 entry: BNEF Energy Storage System Cost Survey 2025: Europe USD 177/kWh turnkey (global 117); NREL Cost Projections for Utility-Scale Battery Storage 2025 Update: 2030 4-h systems 207/279/354 USD2024/kWh; DEA storage catalogue 2030 ~195 EUR/kWh at 4 h; IRENA 2024 actual USD 192/kWh.

life_battery.source: NREL utility-scale battery storage 2025 update explicitly uses a 15-year life with augmentation treated via O&M; DEA projects 20-25 y technical life for 2030 vintages. v6 annualised the battery over 25 years like PV/wind, understating its annual cost ~25%.

life_pv.source: Fraunhofer ISE LCOE 2024 uses 30 y for utility PV; DEA technical lifetime 40 y for 2030 vintages; 25 y is the conservative harmonisation. v6 used 25.

life_wind.source: Fraunhofer ISE LCOE 2024 uses 25 y; DEA technical lifetime 30 y (range 25-35) for 2030 vintages. v6 value retained.

life_h2_storage.units: years, geological H2 storage economic lifetime
life_h2_storage.source: Salt/rock caverns are long-lived civil assets (natural-gas caverns operate for decades); 30 y screening base.

fom_battery.units: fraction of battery capex per year
fom_battery.source: NREL 2025 battery report: fixed O&M ~4% of power-basis capex including augmentation; on an energy-basis capex for 4-h systems this is ~2.5%/y. Base retained from v6.

electrolyser_capex_usd_per_kw.units: per kW(e), system EPC-exclusive direct cost at multi-hundred-MW scale (the model's balance-of-plant, owner and contingency multipliers are applied ON TOP; installed-equivalent base ~1670 EUR/kW)
electrolyser_capex_usd_per_kw.source: 2050 OVERLAY: DEA 2050 system 300 EUR2020/kW at 100 MW (275 at 1 GW) ~ 360 EUR2024; Seymour 2050: 358 EUR/kW; IRENA <200 USD/kW target; max keeps IEA-style installed-cost conservatism. Direct-cost basis as in 2030 (model adds indirects). EUR2024. || 2030 entry: IEA Global Hydrogen Review 2025 Assumptions Annex: 2030 installed (incl. electric equipment, gas treatment, plant balancing, EPC) 1400-1820 USD2024/kW global (2024 actual 2000-2600; China 600-1200); JRC/European Hydrogen Observatory: current EU 100-200 MW projects 2630-3050 EUR/kW installed, system (stack+BoP) alone ALK ~1016 / PEM ~1209 EUR/kW; Clean Hydrogen JU SRIA 2030 factory targets ALK 400 / PEM 500 EUR/kW; Fraunhofer ISE bottom-up system 400-500 EUR2021/kW with installed ~2x system. v6 used IEA GHR2024 installed figures as if they were direct costs and then applied indirect multipliers again (double count).

stack_replacement_frac.units: fraction of installed electrolyser capex per replacement
stack_replacement_frac.source: 2050 OVERLAY: Longer stack lives / cheaper stacks by 2050 (SRIA 100,000 h target). || 2030 entry: DOE Hydrogen Program Record 24005: PEM stack replacement 11% of total installed capital; IRENA Green Hydrogen Cost Reduction: stack 30-45% of (uninstalled) system cost. 2030 base 20% of installed.

stack_life_years.units: years (calendar interval between replacements; ~80,000 operating hours at 8,000 h/y full-load-equivalent)
stack_life_years.source: IEA GHR uses 50,000 h economic stack life (stacks reach ~95,000 h); IRENA: ALK 60,000 h, PEM 50,000-80,000 h today, 100,000 h target. Flexible (part-load) operation extends the calendar interval; 10 y base retained.

dac_capex_usd_per_tco2_year.units: per (tCO2/year) of capture capacity, low-temperature solid-sorbent DAC
dac_capex_usd_per_tco2_year.source: 2050 OVERLAY: Fasihi et al. 2019 base trajectory: 199 EUR2019/(t/y) by 2050 (=~240 EUR2024); DEA 2050: ~460 EUR2020/(t/y) as conservative bound; Breyer high-learning ~150. EUR2024. || 2030 entry: Fasihi, Efimova & Breyer 2019 (J. Cleaner Prod.): LT-DAC 730 EUR2019/(t/y) in 2020, falling to 338 (conservative) by 2030; Seymour et al. 2024 adopt 730 EUR2019/(t/y) for 2030 (= ~880 EUR2024, taken as base); max ~1500 EUR2019 (~1820 EUR2024) reflects FOAK evidence (Young et al. 2023 One Earth: FOAK S-DAC levelised 1300-3100 USD/t; Sievert, Schmidt & Steffen 2024 Joule: mature S-DAC ~374 USD/t only at Gt-scale). v6 min of 100 was below any published 2030 estimate and is removed.

dac_electricity_kwh_per_tco2.units: kWh(e) per tCO2, LT solid-sorbent DAC (fans, controls, vacuum)
dac_electricity_kwh_per_tco2.source: 2050 OVERLAY: Fasihi 2050: 182 kWh_el/t (confirmed via Frontiers in Climate 2024); DEA 2050: 280 kWh/t. || 2030 entry: Fasihi et al. 2019: 250 kWh/t (2020) -> 225 (2030) -> 203 (2040); Kueng et al. 2023 (EES, Climeworks co-authored): ~500 kWh/t measured today. v6 used 203 kWh/t, Fasihi's 2040 value; base moves to the 2030 estimate.

dac_heat_kwh_per_tco2.units: kWh(th) per tCO2 at 80-120 C regeneration, LT solid-sorbent DAC
dac_heat_kwh_per_tco2.source: 2050 OVERLAY: Fasihi 2050: 1102 kWh_th/t; DEA 2050: 1500 kWh_th/t. || 2030 entry: Fasihi et al. 2019: 1750 kWh/t (2020) -> 1500 (2030) -> 1286 (2040); IEA Direct Air Capture 2022: S-DAC total 7.2-9.5 GJ/t at 75-80% heat share. v6 used 1283 kWh/t (Fasihi 2040); base moves to the 2030 estimate.

dac_water_recovery_t_per_tco2.units: t H2O co-produced per tCO2 captured (credited against electrolysis water demand)
dac_water_recovery_t_per_tco2.source: IEA Direct Air Capture 2022: S-DAC extracts 0.8-2 t water per tCO2 alongside capture; Fasihi et al. 2019 quote the same Climeworks range. Humidity-dependent; temperate-Europe base 1.0.

ft_capex_usd_per_kw_liquid.units: per kW of full liquid slate output (LHV), direct cost incl. RWGS/syngas preparation and product upgrading/hydrocracking
ft_capex_usd_per_kw_liquid.source: 2050 OVERLAY: Seymour 2050: 452 EUR2019/kW (~547 EUR2024, optimistic min); DEA Hydrogen-to-Jet 2050: 957 EUR2020/kW (~1150 EUR2024) at small 260 MW reference. Base 700 EUR2024 mid. EUR2024. || 2030 entry: Seymour et al. 2024: FT incl. RWGS + refining 799 EUR2019/kW (2030) = ~967 EUR2024/kW; ICCT Zhou & Searle 2022: 450 USD2020/kW; Concawe 17/22 small-reference-scale (27.8 MW) train 1500-1800 EUR/kW marks the max. v6 base 1600 reflected small/FOAK trains and is roughly 2x the nth-of-a-kind literature at the model's ~2 GW-liquid scale.

ft_energy_efficiency.source: 2050 OVERLAY: Seymour 2050: 80%; DEA 2050: 75%; base 0.78. || 2030 entry: ICCT 2022: 73%; Seymour et al. 2024: 65% (2030) rising to 80% (2050); Koenig et al. 2015 detailed flowsheet: 67% H2-to-liquids. v6 used 0.7667 (upper-middle of the band).

jet_energy_share.units: fraction, kerosene share of the upgraded FT liquid slate by energy
jet_energy_share.source: UBA/LBST Power-to-Liquids 2016: jet-suitable share 50-60% by energy; ICCT 2022 unoptimised slate: 40% kerosene; jet-maximised designs with wax hydrocracking and recycle reach ~70%+. Base retained at 0.57.

electrolyser_kwh_per_kg_h2.units: kWh(e) per kg H2, system level (incl. rectifier and BoP)
electrolyser_kwh_per_kg_h2.source: 2050 OVERLAY: DEA 2050: 69.9% LHV = 47.6 kWh/kg; IRENA 2050 design target <45; IEA conservative ~48-50. || 2030 entry: Clean Hydrogen JU SRIA 2030 targets: ALK and PEM 48 kWh/kg system; Fraunhofer ISE bottom-up 2030: 47.6-49.4 kWh/kg; IEA GHR2025 conservative average 2030: ~52 kWh/kg; DOE Record 24005 US 2022 PEM average 57.5. Base 50 kWh/kg (= 66.7% LHV) is the v6 value, confirmed.

h2_compression_kwh_per_kg.units: kWh(e) per kg H2, electrolyser outlet (~30 bar) to process/storage pressure (~100-200 bar)
h2_compression_kwh_per_kg.source: DOE Hydrogen Program Record 9013: ideal isothermal work 30->200 bar ~0.65 kWh/kg, real large machines at ~55-60% isentropic efficiency; HDSAM-based modelling 0.5-0.6 kWh/kg for smaller ratios. v6 used 0.66 kWh/kg (~the ideal work); base moves to a real-machine 1.0.

co2_compression_kwh_per_tco2.units: kWh(e) per tCO2 from atmospheric capture outlet to synthesis pressure
co2_compression_kwh_per_tco2.source: v6 value retained (consistent with standard multi-stage intercooled compression work to ~30-80 bar); range added for sampling.

heat_pump_cop.units: coefficient of performance for DAC regeneration heat top-up (~100 C sink)
heat_pump_cop.source: v6 value retained; industrial high-temperature heat pumps delivering ~100 C achieve COP 2-3.5 depending on source temperature (IEA Energy Efficiency technology context).

heat_pump_capex_usd_per_kw.units: per kW(e) of heat-pump drive power
heat_pump_capex_usd_per_kw.source: Screening range for large industrial heat pumps; minor cost item. v6 range retained with EUR tag.

compressor_capex_usd_per_kw.units: per kW(e) of compressor drive power (H2 and CO2 process compression), direct cost before the model's indirect multipliers
compressor_capex_usd_per_kw.source: HDSAM/Argonne cost functions (Transition Accelerator 2023): ~1700 CAD2019/kW total capital even at 112 MW scale, 2400-3000 CAD/kW at 1-10 MW; Clean Hydrogen JU SRIA pipeline-compressor 2030 target 650-3500 EUR/kW. v6 value of 260/kW resembled a bare natural-gas machine and was ~6-10x below hydrogen-service evidence.

h2_storage_capex_cavern_usd_per_kwh.units: per kWh H2 (LHV) of working capacity, solution-mined salt cavern (= 17/30/53 EUR per kg H2)
h2_storage_capex_cavern_usd_per_kwh.source: Papadias & Ahluwalia 2021 (IJHE): salt-cavern installed capital <19 USD2019/kg at 3000 t scale, ~25 USD/kg for multi-cavern stores; Clean Hydrogen JU SRIA 2030 target 30 EUR/kg for caverns >3000 t. Applied to countries with salt-cavern potential per Caglayan et al. 2020 (see country_finance.json). v6 single base of 2.4/kWh (80/kg) was 2-3x the cavern evidence.

h2_storage_capex_rock_usd_per_kwh.units: per kWh H2 (LHV) of working capacity, lined rock cavern (= 47/63/180 EUR per kg H2); applied where no salt deposits exist (e.g. Finland, Sweden, Alpine states)
h2_storage_capex_rock_usd_per_kwh.source: Papadias & Ahluwalia 2021: LRC installed capital <44 USD2019/kg at 3000 t scale, ~160 USD/kg at 100 t (levelised ~1.7x salt caverns); Elberry et al. 2021 (IJHE): no salt-cavern potential in Finland/Sweden, steel-lined rock cavern (Skallen, 200 bar) is the proven Nordic design. Above-ground vessels (~500-750 USD/kg) are excluded as uninvestable at 15-20 kt scale.

fom_h2_storage.units: fraction of storage capex per year
fom_h2_storage.source: v6 value retained (geological storage O&M incl. compressor maintenance).

h2_path_efficiency.units: fraction, energy-equivalent efficiency of the store-then-feed H2 path (cavern cycling compression + leakage; no reconversion)
h2_path_efficiency.source: Peng et al. 2025 (Sci. Rep.): cumulative salt-cavern leakage <0.4% over 30 y of cycling; Elberry et al. 2021: 94.9-97.1% storage efficiency incl. auxiliaries; ~1 kWh/kg cycling compression = ~3% of LHV. v6 used 0.90 (pessimistic).

co2_storage_capex_usd_per_tco2.units: per tCO2 of buffer capacity (liquid CO2 tankage)
co2_storage_capex_usd_per_tco2.source: Internal screening assumption retained from v6 (now EUR-tagged and sampled); buffer is sized in days so the total is small (~4 CHF/t SAF).

co2_buffer_days.units: days of CO2 throughput held as plant buffer
co2_buffer_days.source: Screening assumption (v6 base retained, range added).

h2_buffer_days.units: days of H2 throughput held as plant buffer (priced at the same geology-dependent storage cost as the seasonal store)
h2_buffer_days.source: Screening assumption (v6 base retained, range added).

balance_of_plant_frac.source: NETL QGESS cost-estimation methodology: offsites/BoP 15-30% of ISBL for chemical-plant screening estimates. v6 base retained inside the sourced range.

owner_cost_frac.units: fraction (owner's costs: development, land, permitting, spares, preproduction)
owner_cost_frac.source: NETL QGESS: owner's costs ~15% of total plant cost plus preproduction/inventory/financing (~20% all-in). v6 8% was below screening practice; base raised to 12%.

contingency_frac.source: NETL/AACE: project contingency 15-30% for Class 4/5 estimates, process contingency higher for units without full-scale operating history (RWGS, DAC). v6 12% was below the sourced floor; base raised to 15%.

process_opex_frac.units: fraction of process capex per year (fixed O&M excl. stack replacement)
process_opex_frac.source: Fasihi et al. 2019 use 4%/y for DAC; Seymour et al. 2024 use 1-4%/y by component. v6 base retained.

plant_availability.source: 8000 h/y (91.3%) is the standard chemical-plant convention in PtL TEAs (Meurer et al. 2024, Fasihi et al. 2019); ICCT uses 95% for grid-buffered plants. v6 base 0.90 retained.

water_demand_kg_per_kg_h2.units: kg raw water withdrawn per kg H2 (stoichiometric 9 plus demineralisation reject and cooling make-up)
water_demand_kg_per_kg_h2.source: IRENA & Bluerisk, Water for Hydrogen Production 2023: consumption 17.5 L/kg (PEM) and 22.3 L/kg (ALK), withdrawal up to 32 L/kg; practical literature band 20-30 L/kg. New in v7 - water was not costed in v6.

water_cost_usd_per_m3.units: per m3 of demineralised water delivered to the electrolyser (raw industrial supply + treatment)
water_cost_usd_per_m3.source: EurEau Europe's Water in Figures 2026: average European water-services tariff 3.59 EUR/m3 (residential, incl. wastewater - industrial supply typically 1-2.5 EUR/m3); KIT 2025 (Desalination): full-chain ultrapure water 2.3-5.5 EUR/m3; EDI polishing ~0.6 USD/m3. Desert reference cases (SAU/ARE/MAR) should sit mid-to-high in this range (SWRO 0.4-1.5 USD/m3 plus inland delivery; World Bank 2019, DEWA Hassyan 2023 record 0.389 USD/m3).

road_variable_usd_per_tkm.units: per tonne-km, jet fuel by ADR tanker truck, 200-650 km hauls
road_variable_usd_per_tkm.source: Derived from CNR European road-haulage cost studies: full cost 1.19-1.25 EUR/vkm (DE 2021, ES 2023) to 1.5-1.8 EUR/vkm (FR market 2026), +10-30% ADR/tanker premium, ~25 t payload, empty-return factor 1.2-2.0. Base: 1.40 EUR/vkm x 1.5 / 25 t = 0.084 EUR/tkm. v6 min 0.035 implied <0.9 EUR/vkm with no empty running (an Australian benchmark, dropped).

rail_variable_usd_per_tkm.units: per tonne-km, jet fuel in dedicated block trains (tank cars), incl. traction and wagon hire
rail_variable_usd_per_tkm.source: Bundesnetzagentur Marktuntersuchung Eisenbahnen 2023: German rail freight average revenue 4.4 ct/tkm (2022, all traffic incl. single-wagon); ~23 EUR/train-km implies ~2.3 ct/tkm for 1000 t block trains. Mineral-oil unit trains sit between. New in v7 - rail mode was disabled in v6.

rail_terminal_usd_per_tonne.units: per tonne, loading + unloading transfer at rail terminals (both ends)
rail_terminal_usd_per_tonne.source: Internal screening assumption for two liquid-bulk transloads; flagged for replacement with a sourced terminal tariff.

pipeline_capex_usd_per_km.source: ACER Unit Investment Cost Indicators 2026: European 12-16 inch pipelines mean 2.24 / median 2.08 MEUR/km; US benchmarks higher (OGJ 2015-16 ~4.75 MUSD/km). Pipeline only offered above pipeline_min_tonnes_per_year (Concawe 23/6: 84% of European product lines <16 inch; 740 kt/y is below viable dedicated-line scale).

electricity_price_usd_per_kwh_logistics.units: per kWh, grid electricity for pipeline pumping
electricity_price_usd_per_kwh_logistics.source: Eurostat electricity price statistics: EU-27 non-household average 0.1837 EUR/kWh (H2-2025, band IC, excl. VAT). v6 used 0.10 flat.

airport_fee_usd_per_tonne.units: per tonne of fuel delivered: airport receiving, fuel-farm and hydrant infrastructure adder
airport_fee_usd_per_tonne.source: Vienna Airport Entgeltordnung 2026: fuelling infrastructure charge 3.74 EUR/m3 (~4.7 EUR/t at 0.8 t/m3); Perth Airport jet fuel infrastructure charge 1.54 AUc/L (~19 AUD/t, full capex recovery + O&M) marks the max; IATA guidance (~3-5 days cover) implies new-build tankage alone is ~0.5-1 EUR/t annualised. v6 explicitly excluded this term (0); v7 monetises it.

wacc.units: fraction, real pre-tax WACC (uniform fallback when country mode is off)
wacc.source: Uniform fallback re-based to the NW-European renewables range (AURES II survey; UK DESNZ 2025 real pre-tax solar 5.0% / onshore wind 5.8%). Country-specific values in country_finance.json are used by default (wacc_mode=country).

wacc_country_delta.units: additive perturbation applied to the per-country WACC in uncertainty sampling
wacc_country_delta.source: Sampling band covering survey vintage (2019-2021), nominal-to-real conversion and post-2022 rate-environment uncertainty.

wacc_process_premium.units: additive premium on the process-plant WACC over the renewables WACC (technology/offtake risk)
wacc_process_premium.source: Internal screening assumption: first-mover PtL synthesis plants finance above pure renewables; flagged for replacement with a sourced hydrogen-project cost-of-capital estimate.

fixed_land_and_utilities_usd_per_year.source: Internal screening assumption for land lease, utilities, insurance and site services of a ~4 GW-scale PtL complex (~92 USD/t at the 740 kt reference size). Explicit and sampled; flagged for replacement with a sourced value. Restated in USD-2024 (60 MCHF x 1.1362). v8: scales with plant size at exponent fixed_cost_scale_exponent.

coproduct_credit_usd_per_tonne_saf.source: No co-product credit in the base model; retained explicitly at zero. The energy-allocated delivered-cost column provides the comparable figure for allocation-based studies.

airport_terminal_and_tankage_usd_per_yea.units: CHF/year (legacy fixed term; superseded by airport_fee_chf_per_tonne)
airport_terminal_and_tankage_usd_per_yea.source: Retained at zero for backward compatibility; the per-tonne airport adder replaces it.

co2_capture_cost_usd_per_t.units: per tCO2 captured+conditioned at biogenic point sources (blend of amine flue-gas capture at pulp/CHP/WtE with a minor high-purity fermentation/upgrading share)
co2_capture_cost_usd_per_t.source: Onarheim et al. 2017 (IJGGC): pulp mills 52-89 EUR/t avoided (~62-107 EUR2024); bioethanol fermentation 15-35 USD/t (IEA); biogas upgrading 10-70 EUR/t (SEMPRE-BIO 2024/OIES); WtE 50-120 EUR/t (ZWE 2024, Roussanaly 2020). Base 70 EUR reflects the amine-dominated scalable stream.

co2_liquefaction_usd_per_t.units: per tCO2, liquefaction for truck/rail logistics (~15 bar, -28 C; 80-160 kWh/t)
co2_liquefaction_usd_per_t.source: ZEP 2011: 5.3 EUR2009/t at multi-Mt scale (~7 EUR2024); Chen & Morosuk 2021 / UCL 2025: 16-21 USD/t; DEA CCTS catalogue small-scale ~25 EUR/t.

co2_purity_polish_usd_per_t.units: per tCO2, polishing to RWGS/FT feed spec (guard beds; O2/S/NOx attention)
co2_purity_polish_usd_per_t.source: Dieterich et al. 2020 (EES) treat CO2 polishing as guard-bed-level cost embedded in conditioning; assumption band retained explicitly.

co2_transfer_fixed_usd_per_t.source: Stolaroff et al. 2021 (Frontiers): ~2 USD/t staging+loading adder for non-pipeline CO2 logistics.

co2_truck_usd_per_tkm.units: per tCO2 per km, liquid CO2 trucking (50-300 km hauls)
co2_truck_usd_per_tkm.source: Stolaroff et al. 2021: 0.111 USD/t-km cryogenic trucking; Becattini et al. 2024 (ETH): ~1 EUR/t per 10 km European inland rule of thumb.

co2_contractable_share.units: fraction of the mapped national biogenic point-source potential contractable for e-SAF (competition from BECCS/other users, retrofit reality)
co2_contractable_share.source: Screening assumption spread; potential data per country_biogenic_co2.json (BEST/Bioenergy Europe 2025; Rosa et al. 2021 cross-check).

co2_max_haul_km.units: km, maximum economic collection radius for trucked biogenic CO2; beyond it on-site DAC covers the remainder
co2_max_haul_km.source: At 0.12 EUR/t-km a 300 km haul adds ~36 EUR/t - approaching the DAC cost delta; rail/pipeline aggregation beyond this is out of screening scope.

ft_min_load_frac.units: fraction of installed synthesis capacity, minimum continuous load (FT+RWGS turndown)
ft_min_load_frac.source: 2050 OVERLAY: Concawe 2050 planning: 50% minimum part load; KIT projects <20% at scale - min relaxed to 0.3. || 2030 entry: Concawe 24-4 planning assumptions: 80% minimum part load for 2020-2030 cases, 50% for 2050; Seymour et al. 2024 use an 80% floor; KIT pilot demonstrated ~40% with <20% projected at scale (Loewert & Pfeifer 2020). Base 0.5 assumes train-level modularity (idling one of several trains).

product_storage_usd_per_m3.units: per m3 installed, on-site finished-jet tank farm (API 650-class, incl. civil/pumps at base)
product_storage_usd_per_m3.source: IEA 2018 emergency-stockholding: new above-ground tankage 110-150 EUR/m3; Thunder Said: 100-300 USD/m3 tank-only, ~500 USD/m3 (80 USD/bbl) full terminal; CRS: 15-18 USD/bbl large product tanks.

fom_product_storage.units: fraction of tank capex per year
fom_product_storage.source: Pfennig et al. 2023 storage O&M band 1-1.5%/y; terminal practice up to 3%.

ft_scale_exponent.units: capex exponent, FT+RWGS+upgrading within a single train (~<=340 kt/y jet); number-up at 0.92 above
ft_scale_exponent.source: Kreutz et al. 2008: FT synthesis 0.60, syngas processing 0.70, upgrading 0.65; single-train max ~12,500 bbl/d; NETL GTL baseline uses 4 parallel trains at 50,000 bbl/d.

electrolyser_scale_exponent.source: DEA 10/100/1000 MW electrolyser datasheets imply n=0.80 (10->100 MW) and 0.96 (100 MW->1 GW); Reksten et al. 2022 quasi-linear above ~10 MW.

dac_scale_exponent.units: capex exponent, solid-sorbent DAC (container-modular; shared BoP only)
dac_scale_exponent.source: Fasihi et al. 2019 model DAC as modular (learning, not scale); NETL sorbent case is modular adsorber trains.

compressor_scale_exponent.units: capex exponent, process compressors (0.1-30 MW per machine; parallel beyond)
compressor_scale_exponent.source: NETL QGESS CO2-compression exponents 0.61-0.88; Towler & Sinnott centrifugal correlation n~0.6-0.8.

generic_scale_exponent.units: capex exponent, heat pump/buffers/other units (six-tenths class)
generic_scale_exponent.source: Six-tenths rule / NETL QGESS BoP accounts 0.43-0.77.

fixed_cost_scale_exponent.units: exponent for the fixed land/utilities/site-services term vs plant size
fixed_cost_scale_exponent.source: Screening assumption: site services scale sub-linearly.

synthetic_saf_reference_eur_per_tonne_20.source: EASA 2026 Briefing Note (2025 aviation fuels reference prices, ReFuelEU Art. 13): synthetic aviation fuels weighted average EUR 7,520/t, range 6,710-9,525/t.

synthetic_saf_atmospheric_co2_reference_.source: EASA 2026 Briefing Note, synthetic aviation fuel from ATMOSPHERIC CO2 (the DAC pathway this model represents): average EUR 8,625/t, range 7,815-9,525/t. This subcategory, not the all-synthetic average, is the like-for-like comparator.

esaf_2030_first_plants_eur_per_tonne.source: Project SkyPower Insights Report (Oct 2024): unsubsidised levelised e-SAF cost EUR 5,000-8,000/t for 2030 European first plants; long-term floor EUR 3,000-4,000/t.
